title: Native launch continuity
lede: The system launch frame and session restore are now a quiet grouped background that matches Home. The Motion W lockup stays on sign-in, where Apple allows a splash after launch completes.

sections.heading: After-only fixture evidence
sections.note: iPhone 16 Pro (27.0) UDID E055DEBC-12B1-4E0F-BE11-1CFFF4A454DE, WisconsinPerformance launch-view / login. No matched before pair from this checkout: the previous branded still lived in the system UILaunchScreen and the launch-view fixture, and those PNGs were not retained beside the earlier review. The reported 9:30 still is included as a device screenshot at a different pixel size, not as a hash-matched pair.

shots.title: Reported system still
shots.cap: The dark-purple LaunchBackground plus Motion W lockup. This is the system frame Apple says not to brand.

shots.title: Restore in Dark Mode
shots.cap: LaunchView is now system grouped black. Session-checking copy appears only after restore takes long enough. No lockup.

shots.title: Restore in Light Mode
shots.cap: The same continuity background follows appearance mode, matching Home's grouped surface.

shots.title: Sign-in
shots.cap: The crimson scene and Gotham lockup remain here. Apple treats this as splash/onboarding after launch completes.

changes.was: LaunchBackground #140B10 plus a centered LaunchLockup wordmark, which read as a purple splash.
changes.now: UILaunchScreen is a required iOS 27 color-only frame. LaunchBackground matches system grouped (light #F2F2F7, dark #000000). No image.

changes.was: LaunchView continued the crimson scene and raster lockup, so the first SwiftUI frame was also a splash.
changes.now: LaunchView is Color(.systemGroupedBackground) with delayed Checking your session copy. Optimistic sessions still skip it.

changes.was: WindowLaunchStillHost covered the live UI with the same branded still.
changes.now: Inactive snapshots show the live UI. No privacy lock and no splash overlay.

changes.was: Kiosk cold launch and resume used the same Motion W still.
changes.now: Login and password setup keep the crimson lockup. Kiosk launch uses KioskLaunchBackground #0B0B0D; resume is labeled progress on the existing backdrop.

verification: vitest ios-launch-experience (6) and the isolated ios-system-hardening snapshot contract passed. Three other hardening tests fail on unrelated pre-existing session-boundary assertions.

xcodebuild WisconsinKiosk generic iOS Simulator Debug BUILD SUCCEEDED.
WisconsinPerformance PasswordManagerScreenshotUITests testLaunchViewCaptures and testLoginIdentityCaptures passed on iPhone 16 Pro (27.0), including a second launch-view pass in Dark Mode.

notes: The launch-view captures include Checking your session because the fixture waits through the delayed progress reveal. The system UILaunchScreen itself has no spinner or text.
Physical-device app-switcher and managed-iPad kiosk visual proof remain open.
